options.metric: Annual number of pedestrians injured in police-reported crashes
options.reason: Injury counts provide a direct, locally meaningful measure of the annual pedestrian harm burden.
options.answer: Brooklyn recorded 2,835 pedestrian injuries in 2025 versus 3,641 in 2013 (22% fewer), although injuries have risen since 2020; these counts do not account for walking volume.
options.interpretation: This answers how the annual number of pedestrians injured in police-reported Brooklyn crashes changed from 2013, showing a lower total in 2025 but a rebound after the 2020 low. Injury counts are a defensible measure of community harm, but without a measure of pedestrian exposure they cannot establish whether an individual's risk of injury fell, and this framing leaves fatal outcomes separate.

options.metric: Annual number of pedestrians killed in police-reported crashes
options.reason: Fatality counts isolate the most severe pedestrian road-safety outcome and make the year-to-year pattern clear.
options.answer: Brooklyn recorded 39 pedestrian deaths in 2025 versus 30 in 2013 (30% more), so this severe-outcome count does not show improvement.
options.interpretation: This answers whether the annual number of pedestrians killed in police-reported Brooklyn crashes changed from 2013, showing a higher but volatile count in 2025. Fatality counts are a direct measure of severe harm, but without pedestrian exposure they cannot establish individual risk, and this framing does not describe nonfatal injuries.
